S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response within 5 business days of learning of it. A death, serious injury, or active fire presenting an immediate risk to others must be reported as soon as practicable and no later than 24 hours after learning of it. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 10 business days when an incident indicates a material safety risk for their model, and promptly provide any protective instructions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% triggers regulator review and a requirement to submit a corrective-action plan, taking account of sample size, test uncertainty, and other relevant safety evidence. The 5% figure is not by itself a sales prohibition. A model may not be newly sold only if the regulator determines, based on the test results and other safety evidence, that continued sale presents an unacceptable risk; the regulator must allow a reasonable period for corrective action and retesting where appropriate.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed systems must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a local means of safe operation. Manufacturers must provide remote shut-off capability for existing installed units within 6 years of this standard’s effective date, through retrofit or replacement where technically feasible. Where retrofit is not feasible, the manufacturer must document the reason, notify the owner, and provide an equivalent risk-reduction plan for regulator review.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery systems manufactured for sale must include built-in fire suppression. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model’s thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and submit the supporting data and a corrective-action plan. The regulator must assess the rate together with incident severity, data quality, test results, and corrective actions, and may require a recall or other protective measures where warranted.

document.section_notes: S1 imposes strict reporting timelines (24h serious, 5 business days others, 10 business days customer notice). S2 sets a 55°C test and 5% review trigger but no automatic sales ban, with results shared with customers/regulators but not public. S3 requires new units shut-off and 6-year retrofit with feasibility alternative; S4 requires built-in suppression in 36 months. S5 uses an 8/100k trigger for corrective action but recall is discretionary, favoring Halcyon. Red lines on public per-model rates, retrofit <6 years, customer access to results, and suppression <36 months are all respected.
